title: Review: Diffusion and facilitated diffusion; Osmosis and water potential; Active transport, bulk transport and co-transport; Digestion and absorption; Cell surface area and size limits
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for AQA A-level Biology (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: EX04#t4 term and clue written for the game; MB03b#t1 term and clue written for the game; MB02a#t1 term and clue written for the game; MB03a#t2 term and clue written for the game. Questions: EX04#N.3, MB02a#N.7a, MB02b#N.3, MB03a#N.10, MB04#N.3a, MB06#N.9, EX04#N.10, MB02a#N.12, MB03a#N.3a, MB06#N.11a, MB03a#N.6a, MB06#N.12. Some questions repeat from the worlds it reviews.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Assimilation
items.clue: Cells build taken-up molecules into the animal's own molecules and tissues

items.label: Dilution series
items.clue: Set of sucrose solutions of different strengths made from one stock solution.

items.label: Simple diffusion
items.clue: Passive movement of small non-polar molecules such as O₂ between the phospholipids.

items.label: Crenation
items.clue: Shrinking and puckering of the surface of a cell without a wall as water leaves it.

questions.stem: A dog eats meat. At which stage are the amino acids from the meat first inside the dog's body?

options.text: When the meat is swallowed and reaches the stomach
When proteases hydrolyse the meat's proteins in the gut
When the amino acids cross the gut lining into the blood
Only when muscle cells build them into the dog's own protein

questions.explanation: Absorption is the moment the products of digestion get inside. Assimilation comes later.

questions.stem: A potassium channel in a cell membrane is open. Which statement describes the movement of ions through it?

options.text: Potassium ions diffuse through, down their gradient, with no ATP used.
Potassium ions and any other ions of similar size diffuse through the open pore.
Potassium ions are moved through in whichever direction the cell requires.
Potassium ions are carried through using energy from the hydrolysis of ATP.

questions.explanation: The channel gives one specific ion a hydrophilic route through the hydrophobic core. The ions move by facilitated diffusion, down their gradient, with no ATP.

questions.stem: An exchange surface changes: its surface area becomes 3 times as large, the difference in concentration across it becomes 2 times as large, and its thickness becomes 1.5 times as large. By what factor does the rate of diffusion change?
Jam contains so much sugar that most bacteria landing on it cannot grow. Which statement explains this?

options.text: Sugar diffuses into the bacteria until there is enough inside them to poison them.
Water leaves the bacteria by osmosis into the jam, so their cytoplasm shrinks and they cannot grow.
Water enters the bacteria from the jam, so the bacteria swell up and burst.
Their cell walls stop any water from crossing, so the bacteria cannot take in water.

questions.explanation: The jam is far more concentrated than the cytoplasm. Water leaves the cells by osmosis; the contents shrink away from the wall, and without water the cells cannot grow.

questions.stem: Root cells absorb nitrate ions from soil water in which the nitrate concentration is much lower than in the cell. When the roots are deprived of oxygen, nitrate uptake falls sharply. What explains these observations?

options.text: Nitrate is taken up by active transport in the same direction as diffusion but faster, and the lack of oxygen slows the diffusion.
Nitrate is taken up by pumps using ATP from aerobic respiration, so without oxygen the supply of ATP falls and active transport slows.
Nitrate is taken up by pumps using ATP already present in the cell, so removing oxygen must have affected the channel proteins instead.
Nitrate is taken up by facilitated diffusion through channels, which use ATP to move ions across against the gradient.

questions.stem: Shrews are among the smallest mammals. Like larger mammals, they keep their body temperature nearly constant. A shrew must eat much more food per gram of its body mass each day than a deer does. Which statement best explains this difference?

options.text: A shrew's cells are much smaller than a deer's, so each has a higher SA:V and needs more food per gram.
A shrew's small body can store only a little heat, so it must eat often to refill that store.
A shrew uses more energy in total each day than a deer does, because its rate per gram of body mass is higher.
A shrew has a higher SA:V, so it loses heat faster per gram and needs more energy per gram to replace it.

questions.stem: How do epithelial cells of the ileum absorb glucose from the lumen when the glucose concentration inside the cells is already higher than in the lumen?

options.text: Glucose diffuses in through the lipid bilayer down its own concentration gradient
A co-transporter hydrolyses ATP directly to move glucose in against its gradient
Sodium–potassium pumps carry glucose into the cell together with the potassium
A co-transporter moves glucose in with sodium ions moving down their gradient

questions.explanation: Sodium moving down its concentration gradient, kept steep by the pumps, provides the energy to move glucose into the cell against its gradient.

questions.stem: A hypothetical toxin binds to and blocks all of the channel and transport proteins in the plasma membrane of a cell. Which prediction about the cell, immediately after exposure to the toxin, is best supported?

options.text: Its uptake of both glucose and O₂ will stop, since all substances cross through proteins.
Its glucose uptake will not change, since glucose passes freely through the phospholipid bilayer.
Its glucose uptake will rise through other routes to meet the cell's own need for glucose.
Its glucose uptake will fall sharply, while O₂ will still diffuse in across the bilayer.

questions.stem: Two adjacent plant cells have water potentials of −300 kPa (cell A) and −900 kPa (cell B). Which statement describes the net movement of water between them?

options.text: From B to A, because −900 kPa is the larger number, so B has the higher water potential.
There is no net movement, because both water potentials are negative.
From A to B only if the cells use energy to pump it, because water cannot move down a gradient by itself.
From A to B, because water moves from higher to lower water potential.

questions.explanation: −300 kPa is the higher water potential. Water moves from higher to lower water potential, so from A to B, until the two are equal.

questions.stem: A human erythrocyte (red blood cell) has a volume of about 90 µm³ and a surface area of about 135 µm². A sphere with the same volume would have a surface area of about 97 µm². What do these figures show about the adaptation of the erythrocyte?

options.text: The biconcave shape gives it about 40% more room for haemoglobin than a sphere would provide.
Flattening gives it about 40% more surface than a sphere of the same volume, which speeds gas exchange.
The extra surface can only come from the erythrocyte being smaller than a typical sphere-shaped cell would be.
Its ratio of 1.5 is higher than the sphere's ratio of 1.08 because the erythrocyte is the larger of the two cells.

questions.stem: A strip of onion epidermis is mounted in a concentrated sucrose solution and viewed under a microscope. Which statement describes what happens to its cells?

options.text: Water leaves each cell by osmosis and the whole cell, wall included, shrinks and crumples inward, just as an animal cell crenates.
Water leaves each cell by osmosis, the protoplast shrinks and its membrane pulls away from the wall: the cells are plasmolysed.
Water leaves each cell by osmosis and an empty space forms between the wall and the membrane, because the wall lets nothing through.
Water enters each cell by osmosis, because the concentrated solution is hypotonic to them, and the cells become turgid.

questions.stem: A spherical single-celled organism grows from a radius of 10 µm to a radius of 30 µm, keeping its shape. Which prediction is best supported?

options.text: Its SA:V rises to three times the original, so each unit of volume is better supplied.
Its SA:V is unchanged, because its shape has not changed.
Its surface grows ninefold, so supply now easily exceeds its larger needs.
Its SA:V falls to one third, so less surface serves each unit of volume.

questions.explanation: SA:V goes from 0.30 to 0.10 µm⁻¹. Demand grows × 27; supply surface only × 9.
